 Ranabaali’s Overall Business Draws Attention; Vijay Deverakonda Scores in Telugu States
 November 4, 2026 / 08:57 AM IST By Filmy Focus Desk 
 --> 
 | 
 Follow Us 
 | 
 Join Us 
 Join Us 
 Vijay Deverakonda’s Ranabaali has attracted attention for its overall business performance, with reported theatrical collections and non-theatrical deals becoming key talking points.
 According to trade estimates, the film has grossed approximately ₹82 crore worldwide at the box office, while its non-theatrical business is valued at around ₹85 crore. The film has reportedly entered the Super Hit zone across the Telugu states after achieving theatrical recovery in its core markets.
 Ranabaali faced mixed early word of mouth and negative reviews from sections of the overseas reviewing fraternity. Despite the challenging start, the film reportedly received encouraging support in the Telugu states.
 Vijay Deverakonda’s performance and screen presence have been central to the film’s appeal. His physical transformation and commitment to the character helped draw attention to the project.
 The overseas performance, particularly in North America, reportedly remained below expectations. However, the film’s reported performance in Tamil Nadu has attracted interest, with approximately ₹1 crore gross said to have come from the Telugu version alone.
 A simultaneous release in Tamil and Hindi could potentially have expanded the film’s theatrical reach. However, the outcome of such a strategy would have depended on audience reception, release expenditure and market conditions.
 The reported ₹85 crore in non-theatrical business also contributes significantly to the film’s overall commercial picture. Digital, satellite and other rights can provide producers with substantial revenue, though final profitability depends on the complete cost and revenue structure.
 Following Dear Comrade, Kushi and Kingdom, Ranabaali adds another notable box-office talking point to Vijay Deverakonda’s career.
 With a reported ₹82 crore worldwide theatrical gross and ₹85 crore in non-theatrical business, the film’s overall performance highlights the importance of considering theatrical collections, territory-wise recovery and non-theatrical revenue together.
 Note: All box-office and non-theatrical figures are trade estimates and should be verified before publication.
